facts.claim: Claude Code charges by API token consumption; subscription plans (Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise) are offered separately.
Anthropic's Supported Regions Policy lists the countries where its products, including Claude Code, are available; any country not listed is unsupported, and mainland China is not listed.

For consumer plans (Free, Pro, Max, Ultra) Claude Code data may be used to train new models when that setting is on; under commercial terms (Team, Enterprise, API) Anthropic does not train on code or prompts sent to Claude Code unless the customer opts in.
Transcripts shared with Claude Code through /feedback, /bug or /share are retained for 5 years; session transcripts are stored locally in plaintext under ~/.claude/projects/ for 30 days.
Claude Code has an uninstall section for each installation method and a step to remove configuration files.
Codex is included in ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu and Enterprise plans; eligible plans can extend usage with credits and pay-as-you-go.
Codex supports two sign-in methods for OpenAI models: sign in with ChatGPT for subscription access, or sign in with an API key for usage-based access.
Running codex logout clears the stored Codex credentials.
OpenAI's supported-countries page for its API lists the countries and territories where access is supported; mainland China is not on the list.

For Business, Enterprise and Edu accounts OpenAI does not use inputs or outputs from its products to improve models by default; Pro and Plus conversations may be used to improve models unless training is turned off in ChatGPT data controls.
Pi is published under the MIT license.
To use Pi you need access to a model through a supported provider, which can be a subscription, an API key or a local model.
If Pi was installed with npm, it is removed with npm uninstall -g @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent.
Inside Pi, /logout removes a provider's stored credential; it does not unset environment variables or revoke the credential at the provider.
PI_TELEMETRY controls install and update telemetry and provider attribution headers (0, false or no turns them off); PI_OFFLINE disables automatic network activity, including model catalog refreshes.
CodeBuddy has personal Free and Pro plans, each offered as a continuous monthly or annual subscription with monthly credits.
Tencent's CodeBuddy Enterprise Privacy Policy says inputs and outputs are kept for up to fourteen days.
CodeBuddy Code is removed with npm uninstall -g @tencent-ai/codebuddy-code, and its default configuration directory is ~/.codebuddy.

DeepSeek Harness official-model use requires a DeepSeek account; dialogue logs of the agent service are collected, and inputs and outputs may be used to optimise models after de-identification, with an opt-out.
DeepSeek Harness stores personal information within mainland China and states that it does not currently transfer it abroad.
With a custom model in DeepSeek Harness, the model service is provided by the model provider you call, not by DeepSeek Harness.
In DeepSeek Harness you enter a DeepSeek API key under Settings, Models; the key is stored in $DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml.
DeepSeek Harness desktop uninstall: the app is removed by the normal uninstall steps, and clearing local data is optional.
DeepSeek model prices are listed per 1M tokens, and a token is the smallest unit of text the model recognises.
MiniMax Code requires a MiniMax account with available credits or your own compatible model API, and model calls may incur charges; the project is MIT licensed.
MiniMax Code sign-in: a mainland China account uses mcode login, and a Global account uses mcode login --region global.
For an npm installation of MiniMax Code, run npm uninstall -g @minimax-ai/code.
Removing the MiniMax Code npm package leaves user data in place.
Anthropic's Claude Code best-practices guide advises telling the assistant what it cannot see and giving it a check to run.
Claude Code tracks changes from its own edits automatically, and its rewind feature can return files and conversation to an earlier point.
Claude Code checkpoints are not a replacement for version control.
In GitHub Desktop, a commit must include a commit message that briefly describes the changes.
GitHub Desktop shows which lines were added and removed before you commit.
Claude Code checkpoints are not a replacement for version control, and changes made by Bash commands are not tracked by checkpoints.
Anthropic's Claude Code best-practices guide advises giving the assistant a check to run, so it can verify its own work.
In Claude Code, a session's permission mode sets which actions Claude can take without asking you first.
